name: Volcanic & aviation ash
value: Mayon at Level 3; no red aviation codes
summary: No red aviation codes, large eruptions or ash closures found as of 11 Nov; Mayon remains at Alert Level 3
state: Phivolcs raised Mayon to Alert Level 3 after a moderately explosive eruption on 30 Oct (The Star, citing Reuters), and an eruption on 3 Nov sent ash 1,600 m high and left 3,903 people displaced in Albay (Daily Tribune). These are local hazards rather than events disrupting major air routes. No red aviation colour code, VEI 4+ eruption or major ash-related airspace closure was found as of 11 Nov.
for_you: Air travel is not materially affected. Travellers to Albay in the Philippines should follow Phivolcs and local authority guidance on the 6 km danger zone.
rubric_hit: No aviation colour code red and no large eruption = Normal

sources.title: Daily Tribune — Mayon spews ash plume, displaces nearly 4k residents
The Star — Philippines raises volcano alert level as blast sends ash skyward

why: Major eruptions ground flights (Iceland 2010) and can cool the climate for years.
drivers: Volcanic unrest; impact depends on ash plume height and jet-stream direction.

rubric.alert: Major airspace closures from ash, or a VEI 4+ eruption.
rubric.watch: Aviation colour code orange/red at a volcano near major air routes, or a large eruption.
rubric.normal: No aviation colour code red; no large eruptions.
